name: Skin bleaching injections (glutathione IV)

lead: Glutathione is an antioxidant the body makes. Some clinics sell it as intravenous whitening drips, promoted to lighten skin and clear undertones, and Wikipedia describes it as the most common agent taken by mouth to whiten skin. The payoff people want is a lighter, more even skin tone.

It is said to inhibit tyrosinase and shift melanin production toward lighter pigment. A 2016 review in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology concluded that no evidence proves IV glutathione works for skin lightening, and Wikipedia says it is unclear whether glutathione works. In looksmaxxing communities it is sometimes discussed as a way to lighten skin tone or undertones.

paras: It is offered in clinics and spas as a series of IV sessions, alongside oral and topical glutathione products. Any change in tone is described as gradual, with repeat sessions marketed to keep it.

The Philippine drug regulator issued a warning against IV use after adverse effects, and the Philippine government advises against it. The 2016 review found evidence for safety and efficacy limited. People with pigment concerns can ask a dermatologist about options.

angle.text: IV glutathione is sold as a whitening drip, promoted to reduce melanin and give a lighter, more even skin tone. A 2016 review found no evidence proving it lightens skin, and a regulator has warned against IV use.

lead: Glutathione is a small antioxidant molecule made naturally by the body. It is promoted, in oral, topical and intravenous (IV) forms, as a skin-lightening agent, and IV or injected versions are sometimes sold as "whitening drips" [1][2]. Wikipedia describes glutathione as the most common agent taken by mouth to whiten skin [2].

A 2016 review in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology concluded that the evidence for efficacy and safety diverges, that no evidence proves IV glutathione works for skin lightening, and that adverse effects from IV use led the Philippine drug regulator to issue a warning [1]. Wikipedia likewise says it is unclear whether glutathione works and notes that the Philippine government advises against IV use [2]. In looksmaxxing communities it is sometimes discussed as a way to lighten skin tone or undertones.
infobox: Lighter skin tone via reduced melanin production
Philippine authorities warn against IV use [1][2]

paras: The review states that glutathione's lightening effect is attributed to direct and indirect inhibition of the enzyme tyrosinase and to a shift from eumelanin (dark pigment) to phaeomelanin (lighter pigment) production [1].

The 2016 review found a gap between how widely IV glutathione is used and the evidence supporting it, stating that no evidence proves efficacy for skin lightening and raising the possibility that its promotion is commercially driven [1]. Wikipedia says whether glutathione works remains unclear as of 2019 and lists it among whiteners that may contain harmful ingredients [2].

Skin lightening is widespread in parts of Asia, Africa and elsewhere, and glutathione is among the products used [2]. A forum thread on looksmax.org asks whether glutathione injections clear skin undertones, with one poster reporting that their eyes looked lighter after a first IV session.

No studies found establishing efficacy of IV glutathione for skin lightening; the 2016 review states that no evidence proves it [1]. Registered trials involving glutathione concern other conditions, such as gingival hyperpigmentation [3].
